question: Find the value of K if the following system of equations fail to have a unique solution: $Kx + 3y - z = 1$; $x + 2y + z = 2$; $-Kx + y + 2z = -1$
explanation:
The system fails to have a unique solution when the determinant of coefficient matrix is zero.

Coefficient matrix: $\begin{bmatrix} K & 3 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ -K & 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$

$\Delta = K(4 - 1) - 3(2 + K) - 1(1 + 2K)$

$= K(3) - 3(2 + K) - (1 + 2K)$

$= 3K - 6 - 3K - 1 - 2K$

$= -7 - 2K$

Set $\Delta = 0$:

$-7 - 2K = 0$

$2K = -7$

$K = -\frac{7}{2}$
